LESSON: SWIMMING (OPTIONAL)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.5: Swimming (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swimming (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why are swimming skills considered as survival skills?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the body position in breaststroke,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform breaststroke in swimming for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge own and others’ efforts while performing breast stroke skills in swimming.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swimming (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the body position in breaststroke,

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. perform breaststroke in swimming for skill acquisition,

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge own and others’ efforts while performing breast stroke skills in swimming.

   Swimming (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  watch a virtual or actual performance to observe breaststroke in swimming, Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.  demonstrate breaststroke skill, Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  watch a virtual or actual performance to observe breaststroke in swimming, Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.  demonstrate breaststroke skill, Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swimming (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Self-efficacy: developed when the learner expresses water confidence as they practise the skill of breaststroke and provide

feedback to each other about the performance.

 Learning to learn: the learner acquires new skill of breaststroke while practising in the swimming pool.

37

Values:
 Unity: The learner displays team spirit while applying the skills of breaststroke.

 Responsibility: The learner carries out the practice of breaststroke while observing own and others safety.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Safety: The learner observes safety measures as they practise breaststroke during swimming.

 Life skills: The learner acquires swimming skills as survival skills in case of emergencies such as floods.

Link to other learning areas:

Integrated Science: The learner uses the knowledge of floatation to perform breaststroke in swimming..

Main points to remember:

1. describe the body position in breaststroke,
2. perform breaststroke in swimming for skill acquisition,
3. acknowledge own and others’ efforts while performing breast stroke skills in swimming.

Remember the key question: Why are swimming skills considered as survival skills?
